questions.title: Symbol String Cast
questions.description:
Read a symbol name from stdin, build a Symbol object from it, then print its String representation.

Input Format:
A single line containing a symbol name (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The string form of the symbol (no leading colon).

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
sym = name.to_sym
puts sym.to_s

questions.title: String to Symbol Cast
questions.description:
Read a string from stdin and print its Symbol form so the leading colon is visible.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The Symbol form including a leading colon, e.g. ":hello".

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
puts name.to_sym.inspect

questions.title: Inclusive Range Printer
questions.description:
Read two integers a and b and print every integer in the inclusive range a..b, one per line.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Each integer from a to b (inclusive) on its own line.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
(a..b).each { |n| puts n }

questions.title: Status Code Symbol Printer
questions.description:
A traffic light controller maps numeric codes to status symbols. Read an integer code (1, 2 or 3) and print the matching status string ("active", "paused" or "stopped"). Use a case/when that yields symbols internally.

Input Format:
A single line containing an integer code.

Output Format:
The status string corresponding to the code.

Constraints:
code is one of 1, 2 or 3
questions.sourcecode:
code = gets.to_i
status = case code
when 1 then :active
when 2 then :paused
when 3 then :stopped
else :unknown
end
puts status.to_s

questions.description:

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
An integer — the sum a + (a+1) + ... + b.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
total = 0
(a..b).each { |n| total += n }
puts total

questions.title: Symbol Lookup in List
questions.description:
A small palette tool checks whether a color symbol is registered. Read a color name, convert it to a Symbol, then print "yes" if it is in the palette [:red, :green, :blue] and "no" otherwise.

Input Format:
A single line containing a color name (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The string "yes" or "no".

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
target = name.to_sym
colors = [:red, :green, :blue]
puts colors.include?(target) ? "yes" : "no"

questions.title: Page Range Even Sum
questions.description:
A report generator sums the even page numbers in a chapter. Read two integers a and b, iterate the inclusive range a..b with each, and print the sum of even numbers in that range. Do not use step, select, reject or sum.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
An integer — the sum of even numbers in a..b.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def even_sum(a, b)
  total = 0
  (a..b).each do |x|
    if x % 2 == 0
      total += x
    end
  end
  total
end

a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts even_sum(a, b)

questions.title: Exclusive Range Skip Last
questions.description:
A book club lists the books they will read this month — every ID from a up to but not including b. Build the list manually with each and join it as a comma-separated string. Do not use step, first, drop or last.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
A comma-separated list of the integers in a...b.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a < b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def exclusive_range(a, b)
  result = []
  (a...b).each { |x| result << x }
  result
end

a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts exclusive_range(a, b).join(",")

questions.title: Symbol Status Lookup
questions.description:
A status registry exposes the symbols :active, :paused and :stopped. Read a status name (string), convert it to a Symbol, then search the registry manually with each (do not use include?, index or member?) and print "found" or "not found".

Input Format:
A single line containing a status name.

Output Format:
The string "found" if the symbol exists in the registry, otherwise "not found".

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
def status_lookup(name)
  target = name.to_sym
  list = [:active, :paused, :stopped]
  found = false
  list.each do |s|
    if s == target
      found = true
      break
    end
  end
  found ? "found" : "not found"
end

name = gets.chomp
puts status_lookup(name)

questions.title: Range Min Max Finder
questions.description:
A statistics helper computes both ends of an inclusive range using Range methods. Read two integers a and b and print the minimum and maximum values of the range a..b separated by a space. Do not use sort, first or last.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Two integers separated by a single space — the min and the max.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def range_stats(a, b)
  r = (a..b)
  "#{r.min} #{r.max}"
end

a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts range_stats(a, b)

questions.title: Step Range Printer
questions.description:
A metronome ticks at a fixed step within a beat range. Read three integers a, b and s and print every s-th integer in the inclusive range a..b, space-separated. Use Range#step; do not use select, reject or map.

Input Format:
A single line containing three space-separated integers a, b and s.

Output Format:
Space-separated integers that the step iteration yields.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000; 1 <= s <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def step_range(a, b, s)
  result = []
  (a..b).step(s) { |x| result << x }
  result
end

a, b, s = gets.split
puts step_range(a.to_i, b.to_i, s.to_i).join(" ")

questions.title: Symbol Hash Key Lookup
questions.description:
A login table maps username symbols to user ids. Read a username string, convert it to a Symbol and search the hash manually with each (do not use include?, fetch, dig or Hash.new with default). Print the user id when found, otherwise "missing".

Input Format:
A single line containing a username (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The user id (integer) for the username, or "missing".

Constraints:
1 <= username length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
def lookup(name)
  table = { alice: 1, bob: 2, carol: 3 }
  target = name.to_sym
  result = "missing"
  table.each do |k, v|
    if k == target
      result = v
      break
    end
  end
  result
end

name = gets.chomp
puts lookup(name)

questions.title: Range Palindrome Prime Counter
questions.description:
A number theorist counts integers in a range that are both prime and palindromic (read the same forwards and backwards). Read two integers a and b and iterate the inclusive range with each. Implement primality and palindrome checks manually with while loops; do not use Prime, prime?, select or count.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
An integer — the number of palindrome primes in a..b.

Constraints:
1 <= a <= b <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def is_prime(n)
  return false if n < 2
  i = 2
  while i * i <= n
    return false if n % i == 0
    i += 1
  end
  true
end

def is_palindrome(n)
  s = n.to_s
  i = 0
  while i < s.length / 2
    if s[i] != s[s.length - 1 - i]
      return false
    end
    i += 1
  end
  true
end

def count_palindrome_primes(a, b)
  count = 0
  (a..b).each do |n|
    if is_prime(n) && is_palindrome(n)
      count += 1
    end
  end
  count
end

a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts count_palindrome_primes(a, b)

questions.title: Symbol Frequency Tally
questions.description:
A tag analyzer reads a line of words, converts each to a Symbol, and prints each distinct symbol with its frequency sorted alphabetically by the symbol's string form. Implement counting manually with each_char; do not use tally, group_by, count or inject.

Input Format:
A single line containing words separated by single spaces.

Output Format:
One line per distinct symbol: "<symbol> <count>" sorted alphabetically by the symbol's string form.

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 500
questions.input2: x y z x y x
questions.sourcecode:
def gather_symbols(line)
  counts = {}
  word = ""
  line.each_char do |c|
    if c == " "
      unless word.empty?
        sym = word.to_sym
        counts[sym] = (counts[sym] || 0) + 1
        word = ""
      end
    else
      word += c
    end
  end
  unless word.empty?
    sym = word.to_sym
    counts[sym] = (counts[sym] || 0) + 1
  end
  counts
end

line = gets.chomp
counts = gather_symbols(line)
result = counts.map { |k, v| [k, v] }.sort { |a, b| a[0].to_s <=> b[0].to_s }
result.each do |sym, n|
  puts "#{sym} #{n}"
end

questions.title: Range Sum of Squares Filter
questions.description:
An energy calculator sums the squares of integers in a range that are divisible by a given factor. Read three integers a, b and k and print the sum of squares (n*n) of integers n in a..b where n is divisible by k. Iterate with each on the inclusive range; do not use select, reject, sum, Math methods or the ** operator.

Input Format:
A single line containing three space-separated integers a, b and k.

Output Format:
An integer — the filtered sum of squares.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= b <= 1000; 1 <= k <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def sum_of_squares(a, b, k)
  total = 0
  (a..b).each do |n|
    if n % k == 0
      total += n * n
    end
  end
  total
end

a, b, k = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts sum_of_squares(a, b, k)

questions.title: Exclusive Range Interval Intersector
questions.description:
A scheduler computes the overlap of two time windows represented as exclusive integer ranges (a...b) and (c...d). Read four integers and print the integers that fall in both ranges, space-separated, in ascending order. Iterate the first range with each and test membership in the second range using include?; do not use Set, intersection, & or union.

Input Format:
A single line containing four space-separated integers a, b, c and d.

Output Format:
Space-separated integers in the intersection (ascending). If the intersection is empty, print nothing (the test cases always have a non-empty intersection).

Constraints:
-1000 <= a < b <= 1000; -1000 <= c < d <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def intersect(a, b, c, d)
  result = []
  (a...b).each do |x|
    if (c...d).include?(x)
      result << x
    end
  end
  result
end

a, b, c, d = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts intersect(a, b, c, d).join(" ")
